From aa69918bd418e700309fdd08509dba324fb24296 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ilya Maximets <i.maximets@ovn.org>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 01:38:37 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] openvswitch: vport: fix self-deadlock on release of tunnel
 ports

vports are used concurrently and protected by RCU, so netdev_put()
must happen after the RCU grace period.  So, either in an RCU call or
after the synchronize_net().  The rtnl_delete_link() must happen under
RTNL and so can't be executed in RCU context.  Calling synchronize_net()
while holding RTNL is not a good idea for performance and system
stability under load in general, so calling netdev_put() in RCU call
is the right solution here.

However,
when the device is deleted, rtnl_unlock() will call netdev_run_todo()
and block until all the references are gone.  In the current code this
means that we never reach the call_rcu() and the vport is never freed
and the reference is never released, causing a self-deadlock on device
removal.

Fix that by moving the rcu_call() before the rtnl_unlock(), so the
scheduled RCU callback will be executed when synchronize_net() is
called from the rtnl_unlock()->netdev_run_todo() while the RTNL itself
is already released.

Fixes: 6931d21f87bc ("openvswitch: defer tunnel netdev_put to RCU release")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Acked-by: Eelco Chaudron <echaudro@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Ilya Maximets <i.maximets@ovn.org>
Acked-by: Aaron Conole <aconole@redhat.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260430233848.440994-2-i.maximets@ovn.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/openvswitch/vport-netdev.c b/net/openvswitch/vport-netdev.c
index a92ca8b37f96..c42642075685 100644
--- a/net/openvswitch/vport-netdev.c
+++ b/net/openvswitch/vport-netdev.c
@@ -208,9 +208,13 @@ void ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy(struct vport *vport)
 	 */
 	if (vport->dev->reg_state == NETREG_REGISTERED)
 		rtnl_delete_link(vport->dev, 0, NULL);
-	rtnl_unlock();
 
+	/* We can't put the device reference yet, since it can still be in
+	 * use, but rtnl_unlock()->netdev_run_todo() will block until all
+	 * the references are released, so the RCU call must be before it.
+	 */
 	call_rcu(&vport->rcu, vport_netdev_free);
+	rtnl_unlock();
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy);
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies only one file, `net/openvswitch/vport-netdev.c`, in the `ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy()` function. The change reorders two lines:

- **Before (incorrect order):**  
  `rtnl_unlock();`  
  `call_rcu(&vport->rcu, vport_netdev_free);`

- **After (fixed order):**  
  `call_rcu(&vport->rcu, vport_netdev_free);`  
  `rtnl_unlock();`

**Relationship:**  
The bug is a self-deadlock when removing tunnel ports. The original code called `rtnl_unlock()` first, which internally triggers `netdev_run_todo()` – this waits for all references to the net_device to be released. However, the RCU callback that actually decrements the reference (`vport_netdev_free`) was scheduled *after* the unlock, so the wait never completes, causing a deadlock. By moving `call_rcu()` before `rtnl_unlock()`, the RCU callback is scheduled while RTNL is still held. The lock is then released, and `netdev_run_todo()` can proceed while the RCU callback is eventually executed during the same grace period, breaking the deadlock. This single reordering fixes the issue without requiring additional synchronization.

Here is the root cause:
The bug is a self-deadlock caused by calling rtnl_unlock() before scheduling the RCU callback (via call_rcu()) that releases the net_device reference. rtnl_unlock() triggers netdev_run_todo() which blocks until all references are released, but the callback (vport_netdev_free) is only scheduled after that point, so it never executes and the deadlock occurs.

Here is the patch:
 
 void ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy(struct vport *vport)
 {
 	rtnl_lock();
 	if (netif_is_ovs_port(vport->dev))
 		ovs_netdev_detach_dev(vport);
 
 	/* We can be invoked by both explicit vport deletion and
 	 * underlying netdev deregistration; delete the link only
 	 * if it's not already shutting down.
 	 */
 	if (vport->dev->reg_state == NETREG_REGISTERED)
 		rtnl_delete_link(vport->dev, 0, NULL);
-	rtnl_unlock();
 
+	/* We can't put the device reference yet, since it can still be in
+	 * use, but rtnl_unlock()->netdev_run_todo() will block until all
+	 * the references are released, so the RCU call must be before it.
+	 */
 	call_rcu(&vport->rcu, vport_netdev_free);
+	rtnl_unlock();
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy);
